**Analysis of the image:**

- **Plant type**: Wheat (narrow grass-family leaves)
- **Affected part**: Leaf blades
- **Key visual features**:
  - Small, discrete, round-to-oval **orange/rust-colored pustules** scattered across the leaf surface
  - Pustules appear randomly distributed (not arranged in stripes or rows)
  - Surrounding chlorotic (yellow) halos around some pustules
  - Pustules appear primarily on the upper leaf surface
  - Multiple leaves affected at similar growth stage near the base

**Reasoning through candidate diseases:**

- **Stripe Rust**: Ruled out — pustules in stripe rust are arranged in distinct yellow stripes along leaf veins; these are randomly scattered
- **Wheat Stem Rust / Stem Rust**: Ruled out — stem rust pustules are larger, brick-red/dark, and appear on stems and sheaths
- **Tan Spot**: Ruled out — tan spot produces tan/brown blotchy necrotic lesions with yellow halos, not discrete raised pustules
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Ruled out — produces irregular tan-brown lesions, not small round pustules
- **Wheat Leaf Rust**: Strong match — classic small, round, orange-brown urediniospore pustules randomly scattered on the upper leaf surface with surrounding chlorosis. Caused by *Puccinia triticina*.

The combination of small, circular, orange uredinia randomly distributed on wheat leaf blades is the hallmark signature of **Wheat Leaf Rust**.
